newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Widen on rate dejection.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Widen on rate dejection.

text.p: Australian bond spreads widened against other dollar bloc debt on Wednesday after the market sold off when the Reserve Bank of Australia remained silent at its first opportunity to ease after the July board meeting.
Bonds had rallied strongly at the open, and spreads had extended Tuesday's narrowing, but the market was already losing ground when no rate cut eventuated at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT).

Economic data later in the morning suggesting some strength returning to the economy -- retail sales rose 2.9 percent in May and building approvals were up 2.2 percent in the month -- also dented the hopes of rate cut bulls and kept bonds heavy.
The immediate focus is now on the outcome of the FOMC meeting in the U.S. later on Wednesday.
Steady U.S. rates would be expected to lead to a firm local market, and narrowing spreads, in the first hour of trade on Thursday.

If the RBA remains silent again, analysts felt spreads could widen again as the market, most notably at the short end, further pared back expectations of a rate cut. This left the curve vulnerable to further flattening.
